_about: BeltGuard tool profiles (owner S4 hav-brain). Representative vibration magnitudes for SCREENING ESTIMATES only. Every value records its source. HSE Table 1 'recommended initial value' = the value HSE suggests using when no better data exists for the specific tool. Trigger minutes are planning assumptions to be replaced by measured trigger time. Load with exposure.load_tool_profiles().
label: SCREENING ESTIMATE - not a certified HAV measurement

primary_source.title: HSE, Vibration risk assessment, Table 1 (tool type, range, recommended initial value)
primary_source.note: HSE warns that manufacturers' data may underestimate workplace vibration substantially; use the tool's own declared value or on-tool measurement when available.

tools.name: Impact wrench 1/2" drive
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: impact wrenches, drive size 3/8, 1/2 & 3/4", range 3-6 m/s2, recommended initial value 5 m/s2

lower_vibration_alternative.method: Non-impact hydraulic or battery torque wrench on bracket bolts
lower_vibration_alternative.note: Removes the impulse mechanism; declared below 2.5 m/s2 class

tools.name: Impact wrench 1" drive
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: impact wrenches, drive size 1", range 7-11 m/s2, recommended initial value 10 m/s2

lower_vibration_alternative.method: Hydraulic torque wrench for large fasteners

tools.name: Angle grinder 100-180 mm
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: angle grinders 100-180 mm (small), range 3-10 m/s2, recommended initial value 7 m/s2

tasks.task: Cut out worn skirt or chute-liner fasteners

lower_vibration_alternative.method: Hydraulic nut splitter or bolt cutter for seized fasteners
lower_vibration_alternative.note: No rotating disc, negligible hand-arm vibration; HSE Table 1 also lists flapper discs at 4 m/s2 for finishing

tools.name: Needle scaler (non vibration-reduced)
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: needle scalers, non-vibration reduced, range 12-26 m/s2, recommended initial value 19 m/s2

tasks.task: De-scale corroded idler frames and stringers

lower_vibration_alternative.note: HSE Table 1: 3-8 m/s2, initial value 7 m/s2 instead of 19 m/s2

tools.name: Needle scaler (vibration-reduced)
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: needle scalers, vibration reduced, range 3-8 m/s2, recommended initial value 7 m/s2

tasks.task: De-scale corroded idler frames and stringers

tools.name: Chipping hammer (stone, concrete, rust)
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: chipping hammers, chipping stone, concrete, rust, range 11-22 m/s2, recommended initial value 20 m/s2

tasks.task: Break hardened carryback and spillage from chute or tail-pulley area

lower_vibration_alternative.method: Water or air lance cleaning, or an engineering fix (belt cleaner, chute liner, air cannon) that removes the hand-held chipping task
lower_vibration_alternative.note: Elimination beats a lower-vibration tool in the HSE hierarchy

tools.name: Drill (rotary, standard bit)
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: drills, standard drill bit, range 2-5 m/s2, recommended initial value 5 m/s2

tasks.task: Drill bracket or guard fixing holes in steelwork

lower_vibration_alternative.note: The drill is clamped to the steel, so the hands do not hold it while it runs

tools.name: Hammer drill
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: drills - impact, 5 and 8 mm masonry bit, range 7-13 m/s2, recommended initial value 11 m/s2

tasks.task: Drill anchor holes in a concrete plinth for guard or bracket fixings

lower_vibration_alternative.method: Rig-mounted drilling, or clamp-on fixings that need no drilling
lower_vibration_alternative.note: Check the replacement tool's declared value

tools.name: Breaker hammer
tools.source: HSE Vibration risk assessment, Table 1: breakers, range 7-18 m/s2, recommended initial value 14 m/s2 (demolition or rotary hammers: range 10-21 m/s2, initial value 18 m/s2)

tasks.task: Break out a damaged concrete plinth or hardened spillage

lower_vibration_alternative.method: Remote-controlled demolition machine, or a vibration-reduced breaker on a support arm
lower_vibration_alternative.note: Takes the breaker out of the operator's hands

tools.name: Power jack / belt lifter (hydraulic)
tools.source: Conservative upper bound, not a measurement: hydraulic jacks and belt lifters are not in HSE Table 1 and have no rotating or percussive hand-held mechanism; 2.5 m/s2 is the level below which tools only declare 'less than 2.5 m/s2', and Safe Work Australia's HAV guide says to use 2.5 m/s2 for such declarations

tasks.task: Lift the belt off the idlers for an idler change-out

tools.name: Hydraulic torque wrench (non-impact)
tools.source: Conservative upper bound: non-impact torque tools are declared in the 'less than 2.5 m/s2' class (HSE Vibration risk assessment, manufacturers' declarations); Safe Work Australia's HAV guide says to use 2.5 m/s2 when a declaration is below 2.5

tasks.task: Torque pulley, gearbox or bracket bolts without impact

tools.name: Phone on vibrate (DEMO stand-in for 1/2" impact wrench)
tools.source: DEMO: uses the HSE recommended initial value of the tool it stands in for (impact wrench 1/2", 5 m/s2). The stand-in's own vibration is neither measured nor used.

lower_vibration_alternative.note: Same alternative as the tool it stands in for
